author: Brad Kenagy
title: 2019 Dow Momentum Strategy Picks
text:
This article will be a review of my 2018 Dow stock-picking strategy selections , along with my 2019 strategy picks. I created the strategy to select stocks in the Dow in hopes of outperforming the Dow ( DIA ) as well as the popular "Dogs of the Dow" Strategy. In 2018, my strategy outperformed the Dow and slightly underperformed the Dogs of the Dow.
My Strategy The starting point for my strategy is to look at the dividend growth and stability for all 30 stocks of the Dow. As a secondary set of criteria, I used two simple technical indicators, a moving average and momentum. My method is different from other methods in that it employs both dividend fundamentals and technical analysis, compared to selecting picks based purely on dividend yield like the Dogs or the Dow strategy or just buying the Dow ETF.
*All positions are an equally weighted
Dividend Stability and Growth Criteria
To get my initial list of Dow stocks, I only included stocks that have increased their dividend over the previous 4 quarters and excluded any companies that have cut their dividends. I also exclude companies that kept their dividend flat over the past year.
Technical Criteria
The technical data I use is from the TD Ameritrade ThinkorSwim platform, but also can be found on many other charting websites.
*The chart Scale I used was Weekly.*
Condition 1: The weekly close at the end of the year is less than the 10-period simple moving average.
Condition 2: The stock must have a 52-period momentum value that is positive.
Condition 3: Out of the stocks that meet the first two conditions, select the stocks with the three highest 52-period momentum values.
* Additional Notes: In the case where at least three stocks do not meet both condition 1 and condition 2, as was the case in 2009, use condition 1 and condition 3, and exclude condition 2.
2018 Results In the following table are the average returns of the stocks selected by the strategy for 2018 compared to the Dow, and the Dogs of the Dow [DOD]. For my calculations, I wanted to make sure dividends were included and reinvested, so I used the DRIP returns calculator on DividendChannel.com to get my final total return.
For 2018, the three stocks that met my above dividend and technical criteria were Apple ( AAPL ), Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) and Coca-Cola ( KO ). As I noted in my opening paragraph, my strategy had a mixed performance during 2018. The reason why my strategy did not outperform the Dow by a wider margin or outperform the Dogs of the Dow is that shares of Apple sold off hard after they reached a trillion-dollar market cap. In addition, shares of Johnson & Johnson had a large one-day sell-off of 10% because of a report about the possibility of Johnson & Johnson having prior knowledge of asbestos in baby powder.

Now, onto 2019…
2019 Strategy Picks Using the same strategy I always do, as described above, I eliminated DowDuPont ( DWDP ) from consideration because they have had a flat dividend and have not increased it recently. All the rest of the companies within the Dow showed positive dividend growth year/year.
Using my remaining strategy criteria, I found five stocks that met my criteria for dividend growth, were trading below their 10 period moving average and had positive momentum. My strategy calls for the selection of the three stocks from this group with the highest momentum. Therefore, my three selections for 2019 are McDonald's ( MCD ), Procter & Gamble ( PG ) and Coca-Cola ( KO ).

McDonald's I believe the biggest catalyst for McDonald's in the coming year will be continued growth of the business and continued improvements in margins because of a focus on quality and investments in technology. McDonald's has grown operating cash flows and free cash flow over the past year, and I see no reason why that growth cannot continue because of their 2020 growth plan, which focuses on food quality, customer experience, and value. McDonald's is improving customer service and margins by expanding the number of locations offering delivery from 5,000 to 9,000 and the continued installation of self-service ordering Kiosks. McDonald's calls these systems Experience of the Future (EOTF) projects, and they expect by the end of 2018 to have 7,000 completed. These are important because they are helping to generate increased sales for McDonald's.
EOTF continues to enhance the customer experience by elevating convenience, hospitality, and personalization. We are pleased with our progress and we are seeing the sales lifts we expected.
~ 2020 vision plan
Fortune
Procter & Gamble I believe the biggest catalyst for Procter & Gamble in the coming year will be the implementation of their new organizational structure with the hopes that it improves margins and helps the company improve its focus. The following chart from a recent investor presentation shows that the business will be reorganized into six business units, which will have their own CEO. The new structure will allow Procter & Gamble to react more quickly to changes in consumer preferences and trends. The second part of the reorganization that should be a benefit to Procter & Gamble is the removal of costs from the business. The costs being removed are labor costs, but other costs as well like a simplified distribution & manufacturing structure. Finally, it is hard to dislike a company that has increased their dividend for 60+ years in a row.
Procter & Gamble investor presentation
Coca-Cola I believe the biggest catalysts for Coca-Cola in the coming year will be continued growth in cash flows and the integration of acquisitions the company has made. Looking at the financials, operating cash flows were up in Q3 2018 vs. Q3 2017. This was the first time in the last four quarters where Coca-Cola has posted higher operating cash flows year/year, which shows that some of their growth initiatives could be taking hold. A recent acquisition that Coca-Cola is in the process of closing is its purchase of Coffee chain Costa, which is Britain's largest coffee chain. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2019 and continues a strategy of diversifying its business away from soda into areas of higher growth like Coffee. Once the deal closes, the press release announcing the deal shows that Costa generated $312 million in EBITDA for its most recent fiscal year.
